v3.title: v3 · truth fixes
v3.summary: v2 with the statements the outside review found untrue or misleading corrected. Nothing new is added except the Whitworth half-turn times, which replace a misleading fact.
changes: “Turn together, so they stay parallel” now says only that the angle between them never changes, and names a parallel pair of lines only when there is one (wiper: P-T stays parallel to Q-U).
A body that keeps its orientation says whether it moves in a straight line or along an arc (wiper CD: curvilinear translation, not a straight line; Scotch yoke CD: straight line).

A pin sliding in a moving slot no longer gets stroke times; that “3 s and 3 s” is what made Luna say the Whitworth has no quick return. The slotted link now gives its slow and fast half-turn times (3.65 s vs 2.35 s).
“Nearly straight for X% of the cycle” is measured in time, counting both passes of a back-and-forth path (Chebyshev 46% → 92%).
A parallelogram is checked against the coupler actually keeping its angle; a crossed one would be called an antiparallelogram.
Dropped two unproven causes: “because the input is not at its pivot” and “when one end rises the other falls” (now: the ends move in opposite directions).
A drawing the solver cannot solve is described as unsolved as drawn, not as a mechanism that cannot move (no template here hits this).

v4.title: v4 · jobs, family check, schematic filmstrip
v4.summary: The app does more of the reasoning and says it in the app's words; the picture is the app's own Schematic drawing at four moments; the prompt asks for a glossary with meanings and for the specific machine the mechanism resembles.
changes: Links and their jobs: every link is named for its job (input crank, coupler, rocker, beam, slotted link, yoke, connecting rod, slider), and each rocker's and slider's two ends are keyed to the input's angle, e.g. “reaches its ends when link AB is at 26 deg and 192 deg”. The same list is the panel's Links table.

Family check: PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog (crank-rocker and the other Grashof classes, parallelogram, slider-crank, Scotch yoke, Whitworth and slotted-lever quick returns, Chebyshev, Roberts, Hoeken and Watt straight-line linkages, Jansen, walking beam, crank-rocker driving a parallelogram, cylinder-driven lever) and names the chain type (Watt or Stephenson six-bar). The note may say “This mechanism is a …” only for a match.

The picture is the app's Schematic style, captured from the drawing-styles build at four moments (a full turn's quarters, or a back-and-forth's two ends and two points between), with authored link names hidden because they give the answer away (“Wiper arm”, “Hood”).
The sheet leads with what matters (at a glance, family, jobs) and puts coordinates last; long per-body length lists are trimmed to the lengths between connecting joints.
“This mechanism” throughout, in the sheet and in the note; the note never mentions the fact sheet or the picture.
Terms come with a meaning, which the panel shows on hover; uses may be fewer than two, and should be what the type is best known for.
After the app's family, the note names the specific machine it strongly resembles, if any: “a Stephenson six-bar that resembles a car hood hinge”.

pairs.name: Four-Bar
pairs.blurb: A classic crank-rocker: a crank turns, a rocker swings, and the coupler between them draws a curve.

answer.plainEnglish: This is a crank-rocker four-bar. **AB** makes full turns about fixed joint **A**, carrying **B** around a circle. **BC** connects the crank to **CD** and rocks as the floating coupler changes angle; **CD** swings back and forth about fixed joint **D**. In this drawing, **BC** rocks through 63.4 degrees, while **CD** rocks through a wider 107.9 degrees, turning the continuous input into an oscillating output.

useCases.why: The full-turn crank and rocking output link suit driving a wiper back and forth.
The oscillating output link can move a screen repeatedly through an arc.

### Structure
- Rigid bodies (moving links): 3.

- link AB lengths: A-B 2.96.
- link BC lengths: B-C 5.75.
- link CD lengths: C-D 3.74.
### Input
- rotary drive at joint A, turning link AB relative to the ground; speed 10 rpm clockwise.
### Solved motion
- Degrees of freedom: 1. Solved 361 samples over 6 s.
- The input runs continuously; the whole motion repeats once per input revolution.
- link AB turns full revolutions about ground pivot A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BC rocks (no fixed pivot: a floating coupler) through 63.4 deg (from 5.9 to 69.4 deg); one way takes 3.53 s and the other 2.47 s (time ratio 1.43).
- link CD rocks about ground pivot D through 107.9 deg (from -111 to -3.1 deg); one way takes 3.23 s and the other 2.77 s (time ratio 1.17).

- C: circular arc of radius 3.74 about D, sweeping 107.9 deg back and forth.

- Four-bar loop: link AB (A-B) 2.96, link BC (B-C) 5.75, link CD (D-C) 3.74, ground A-D 6.48. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link AB (A-B) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 9.44 vs the other two = 9.49).

answer.plainEnglish: This is a crank-rocker four-bar: the driven **AB** makes full turns around fixed joint **A**, carrying floating link **BC** through the loop. That motion makes **CD** swing back and forth around fixed joint **D**. In this drawing, the ground pivots **A** and **D** are 6.48 cm apart. The two moving bars therefore have different jobs: **AB** keeps rotating, while **BC** transfers motion to the rocking output **CD**.

useCases.why: A continuously rotating input can drive an output link that swings back and forth, as **CD** does here.
The rotating **AB** and rocking **CD** show how a four-bar can convert continuous rotation into a repeated swing.

pairs.name: Slider-Crank
pairs.blurb: Rotation into a straight push — the engine and the pump both live here.

answer.plainEnglish: This is an offset slider-crank. **AB** rotates fully around fixed joint **A**, carrying **B** in a circle; rod **BC** connects **B** to slider **C** and makes it move back and forth along its guide. The guide is offset from **A**, so the two strokes take different times: in this drawing’s motion, the slider’s return takes 3.3 seconds and the other stroke takes 2.7 seconds. The coupler **BC** rocks as it transmits the crank’s rotation to the slider.

useCases.why: The slider’s back-and-forth travel can drive a pump piston.
A slider-crank connects a rotating crank to a piston moving back and forth.
The slider’s reversing travel can move a compressor piston.

- link AB (radius 3 about A) drives link CD through pin B riding in a slot on link CD, which pivots at C, 1 from A. The crank radius is larger than that pivot distance, so link CD turns fully but unevenly, fast on one half-turn and slow on the other (the rotating-slotted-link arrangement).

answer.plainEnglish: This resembles a Whitworth quick-return mechanism. **AB** is the input crank, turning steadily around fixed joint **A**. Its pin **B** rides in the slot of **CD**, making **CD** pivot around fixed joint **C** and turn through full revolutions at a changing speed. In this drawing, **A** and **C** are 1 cm apart, and the two slider directions each take 3 seconds, so the motion has no faster return stroke.

rounds.note: Fresh mechanisms: eight library templates not used before, ten mechanisms students sent with feedback (five with a stated goal), and three test cases. Both sides are each version's first asking; v5 was also asked a second time.

Aircraft_Landing_Gear.why: v5 says it looks like an aircraft landing-gear retraction mechanism and names retractable landing gear, in both askings; v4f calls it a triple-rocker four-bar and names no use.

Excavator_Bucket.why: v5 recognizes an excavator bucket linkage in both askings; v4f calls it a cylinder-driven beam mechanism and names no use.

Radial_Engine.why: v5 says a five-cylinder radial engine in both askings; v4f calls it a five-slider slider-crank assembly and names no use.

Oscillating_Fan.why: v5 recognizes an oscillating fan and names pedestal and table fans (its second asking missed it); v4f names windshield wipers.

Elliptical_Trammel.why: v5 names a crossed-slot trammel; v4f says only "two-slider arrangement". (v5's second asking said Scotch yoke, which is wrong.)

Car_Steering.why: v5 says it looks like paired windshield-wiper linkages, in both askings, despite the wheels in the background image: a confident wrong recognition. v4f says nothing wrong.

Toggle_Clamp.why: v4f says it resembles a hand-operated toggle clamp and names toggle clamps; v5's first asking calls it a slow-return crank rocker for power hacksaws (its second asking did say toggle clamp).

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint A turns link AB relative to the ground at 10 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 3 links counting the ground, joined by 2 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: in-line slider-crank. Link AB turns fully and drives slider C along a fixed guide through connecting rod link BC.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A.
- link AB — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground A, at a steady angular speed.
- link BC — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 30.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- slider C — slider on a fixed guide: travels 2.4 back and forth along a fixed guide at 90 deg; it reaches its two ends when link AB's angle (A to B) is 270 deg and 90 deg; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).
### How the parts relate
- Slider-crank: link AB (radius 1.2 about A) drives slider C through rod link BC (length 4.6, 3.83x the crank radius). The guide is in line with the crank pivot, so the two strokes are symmetric.
### Paths of moving points
- B: full circle of radius 1.2 about A.
- C: straight line at 90 deg, length 2.4 (back and forth).
### The picture: this mechanism at six moments, numbered in time order
- 1: 0 s, link AB's angle (A to B) 90 deg.
- 2: 1 s, link AB's angle (A to B) 30 deg.
- 3: 2 s, link AB's angle (A to B) 330 deg.
- 4: 3 s, link AB's angle (A to B) 270 deg.
- 5: 4 s, link AB's angle (A to B) 210 deg.
- 6: 5 s, link AB's angle (A to B) 150 deg.
### Geometry at the start, for reference
- Joints: A (0, 0) ground; B (0, 1.2); C (0, -3.4) slider.
- link AB: A-B 1.2.
- link BC: B-C 4.6.
- Slider C is a pin in a slot (what rides it may turn).

answer.plainEnglish: The driven input turns **AB** all the way around **A**, while **BC** swings and pushes or pulls **slider C** along its fixed vertical guide. The slider travels 2.4 cm back and forth, with equal 3-second strokes in each direction. Because the guide runs through the crank pivot, the slider reaches equal distances on either side of its middle position. This mechanism turns continuous rotation into repeated straight-line motion.

useCases.why: A rotating crank can drive a guided slider back and forth through a connecting rod, as shown by **AB**, **BC**, and **slider C**.
The mechanism's 2.4 cm slider stroke can move a piston repeatedly along a fixed guide.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: the cylinder between A and D, which extends and retracts at 1 cm/s.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The input runs to a limit and reverses, so every part moves back and forth; one full back-and-forth takes 7.61 s.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 4 links counting the ground, joined by 3 pin joints and 2 sliding joints (the cylinder that drives it not counted).
- Matches: cylinder-driven lever. Cylinder A-D, anchored at A, pushes link GDMK at D and swings it about its fixed pivot.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots A, G (apart: A-G 10).
- link GDMK — rocker: rocks about ground G through 40.5 deg; it reaches its two ends when cylinder A-D's length is 4.54 and 8.34; the cylinder pushes it at D.
- link SMT — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 40.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link TU — yoke (carries the slot): slides in a straight line at 90 deg without turning, moving 8.95 back and forth (straight-line translation).
- pin K — pin in a slot: slides 6.53 back and forth within the slot on link TU (motion relative to that link, not an output stroke).
- slider S — slider on a fixed guide: travels 6.53 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when cylinder A-D's length is 8.34 and 4.54.
- cylinder A-D — driven input (a linear actuator); the block marked C on it is the cylinder's own sliding seal, part of the cylinder and not a separate slider: extends and retracts between lengths 4.54 and 8.34 (travel 3.8).
### How the parts relate
- Slider-crank arrangement driven by a rocking lever: link GDMK (arm 8 from its pivot G, swinging 40.5 deg) pushes slider S along its guide through rod link SMT (length 8).
- link GDMK (radius 16 about G) drives link TU through pin K riding in a slot on link TU. link TU cannot turn, so it follows only the part of K's circular motion along its own guide: a steady crank gives it a smooth back-and-forth (harmonic) motion.
- The cylinder pushes link GDMK at D, 6 from its pivot G: 3.8 of extension swings it 40.5 deg, about 10.6 deg per unit of extension.
- link GDMK and link SMT turn as mirror images: equal and opposite angle changes (40.5 deg each).
### Paths of moving points
- D: circular arc of radius 6 about G, sweeping 40.5 deg back and forth.
- M: circular arc of radius 8 about G, sweeping 40.5 deg back and forth.
- K: circular arc of radius 16 about G, sweeping 40.5 deg back and forth.
- S: straight line at 0 deg, length 6.53 (back and forth).
- T: straight line at 90 deg, length 8.95 (back and forth).
- U: straight line at 90 deg, length 8.95 (back and forth).
### The picture: this mechanism at six moments, numbered in time order (1 and 6 are the two ends of its travel)
- 1: 2.1 s, cylinder A-D's length 4.54.
- 2: 2.87 s, cylinder A-D's length 5.3.

- 4: 4.38 s, cylinder A-D's length 6.81.

- 6: 5.91 s, cylinder A-D's length 8.34.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint G turns link GR relative to the ground at 10 rpm clockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
- Traced points: T (on link RST), P (on link KP). The author chose to show these paths, so they are probably the outputs this mechanism exists for.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 8 links counting the ground, joined by 10 pin joints: an eight-bar chain.
- No family in the catalog matched; name it only by what it resembles, if anything.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots G, H, O (apart: G-H 4; G-O 5.39; H-O 9.22).
- link GR — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground G, at a steady angular speed.
- link RST — coupler, carries traced point T: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 40.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link HS — rocker: rocks about ground H through 57.5 deg; it reaches its two ends when link GR's angle (G to R) is 32 deg and 215 deg; one way takes 2.95 s and the other 3.05 s (time ratio 1.03).
- link JKO — rocker: rocks about ground O through 16.5 deg; it reaches its two ends when link GR's angle (G to R) is 286 deg and 134 deg; one way takes 2.53 s and the other 3.47 s (time ratio 1.37).
- link JLT — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 29.1 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link KP — coupler, carries traced point P: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 29.1 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- link LP — coupler: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 16.5 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link GR (G-R) 1.2, link RST (R-S) 3.5, link HS (H-S) 2.5, ground G-H 4. It is a Grashof crank-rocker: link GR (G-R) is the shortest bar, so it is able to turn fully while the opposite side bar only rocks (shortest + longest = 5.2 vs the other two = 6).
- link JKO and link LP turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 16.5 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line J-O stays parallel to line L-P.
- link JLT and link KP turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 29.1 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line J-T stays parallel to line K-P.
- T's path lies overlapping the span of the ground pivots (path x -0.32 to 1.79, y 1 to 3.06; pivots x -5 to 4, y 0 to 2).
- P's path lies overlapping the span of the ground pivots (path x -2.66 to -1.61, y 1.5 to 2.53; pivots x -5 to 4, y 0 to 2).

- R: full circle of radius 1.2 about G.
- S: circular arc of radius 2.5 about H, sweeping 57.5 deg back and forth.
- T (traced): closed curve, 2.11 wide x 2.06 tall, does not cross itself.

- L: closed curve, 1.31 wide x 1.32 tall, does not cross itself; nearly straight for 13% of the cycle over 0.61 (at 56.2 deg, deviation within 0.44% of that length).
- P (traced): closed curve, 1.05 wide x 1.03 tall, does not cross itself.

## Mechanism M1
### At a glance
- Driven input: joint O turns link OAR relative to the ground at 10 rpm counterclockwise.
- Degrees of freedom: 1. The motion repeats every 6 s, once per input revolution.
### Family check (PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog)
- Structure: 5 links counting the ground, joined by 5 pin joints and 1 sliding joint.
- Matches: in-line slider-crank. Link OAR turns fully and drives slider C along a fixed guide through connecting rod link AC.
### Links and their jobs
- ground — frame: fixed pivots O, P (apart: O-P 4).
- link OAR — input crank: turns full revolutions about ground O, at a steady angular speed.
- link AB — translating link: moves along a curve without turning: not in a straight line; every point of it traces the same circular arc as A (radius 0.8 about O), shifted (curvilinear translation).
- link PBS — crank: turns full revolutions about ground P, at a steady angular speed.
- link AC — connecting rod: has no fixed pivot; it swings back and forth through 18.2 deg while it moves (general plane motion).
- slider C — slider on a fixed guide: travels 1.6 back and forth along a fixed guide at 0 deg; it reaches its two ends when link OAR's angle (O to R) is 0 deg and 180 deg; one way takes 3 s and the other 3 s (time ratio 1).
### How the parts relate
- Four-bar loop: link OAR (O-A) 0.8, link AB (A-B) 4, link PBS (P-B) 0.8, ground O-P 4. It is a parallelogram: opposite bars are equal and the coupler keeps its angle, so the coupler stays parallel to the ground line and the two side bars stay parallel to each other.
- Slider-crank: link OAR (radius 0.8 about O) drives slider C through rod link AC (length 5.06, 6.33x the crank radius). The guide is in line with the crank pivot, so the two strokes are symmetric.
- link OAR and link PBS turn together: their angles change identically at every instant (both sweep 360 deg), so the angle between them never changes. Line O-R stays parallel to line P-S.
- link OAR is a lever (beam) pivoted at O between A and R: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.8 and 1.6), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and R moves 2x as far as A.
- link PBS is a lever (beam) pivoted at P between B and S: they sit on opposite sides of the pivot (arms 0.8 and 1.6), so the two ends always move in opposite directions, and S moves 2x as far as B.
### Paths of moving points
- A: full circle of radius 0.8 about O.
- R: full circle of radius 1.6 about O.
- B: full circle of radius 0.8 about P.
- S: full circle of radius 1.6 about P.
- C: straight line at 0 deg, length 1.6 (back and forth).
### The picture: this mechanism at four moments, numbered in time order
- 1: 0 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 270 deg.
- 2: 1.5 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 0 deg.
- 3: 3 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 90 deg.
- 4: 4.5 s, link OAR's angle (O to R) 180 deg.
### Geometry at the start, for reference
- Joints: O (0, 0) ground; A (0, 0.8); R (0, -1.6); B (4, 0.8); P (4, 0) ground; S (4, -1.6); C (-5, 0) slider.

- link AB: A-B 4.
- link PBS: P-B 0.8; P-S 1.6; B-S 2.4.
- link AC: A-C 5.06.
